drug_class: Anticholinergic / Mydriatic and Cycloplegic Eye Drop
purpose: Cyclopentolate is an eye drop used by eye doctors to dilate (widen) your pupils and temporarily relax the focusing muscles in your eyes. It is most commonly used during eye exams so the doctor can get a better look inside your eye. It is also sometimes used to help treat certain eye conditions like inflammation.
how_it_works: Your eye has tiny muscles that control how big your pupil is and how your lens focuses. Cyclopentolate blocks the nerve signals that normally keep those muscles active, causing your pupil to open wide and your eye's focusing ability to temporarily pause. This makes it much easier for your eye doctor to examine the back of your eye and accurately measure your prescription.
common_side_effects: Your vision will be blurry and lights may feel very bright for several hours after use — this is expected. Your eyes may sting or burn briefly right after the drops are put in. You might also notice that reading up close feels difficult until the drops wear off.
warnings: Do not drive or operate machinery until your vision fully returns to normal, which can take 4 to 24 hours. Keep these drops away from children, as accidental swallowing can be very dangerous. Let your doctor know if you have glaucoma or a history of it, since these drops can raise eye pressure. Some people, especially children and the elderly, may experience flushing, fast heartbeat, dry mouth, or confusion — contact your doctor right away if this happens.
typical_dosing: For adults, usually 1 to 2 drops of the 1% solution are placed into the eye(s) about 40 to 50 minutes before an eye exam. For children, a weaker concentration (0.5%) is often used. Your eye doctor or their staff will administer this for you in the office — you generally would not be using this at home on your own.
